tools.name: mttr_sites
tools.description: Lists the sites mttr has read, each with its latest score, page count and the rule to fix first.

tools.name: mttr_site

tools.name: mttr_pages
tools.description: The pages of a site from its latest run, with status, depth, words and the rules each fails. Can be narrowed to the pages failing one rule.

tools.name: mttr_page
tools.description: One page of a site: what it says about itself, the rules it fails with the fix for each, and the pages that link to it and that it links to.

tools.description: Makes JSON-LD for one page from the fields given, as the free schema creator does, and fetches nothing. tools.description: Grades a brand's location pages together, the free multi-location grader: robots.txt asked first, so a site closed to mttr is not read; then its home page and sitemap, and up to 25 location pages, state and city listings followed down to the places and subpages every location has left out. tools.description: Checks one public host's SSL certificate, the free SSL certificate checker: one TLS handshake on port 443 with the name sent as SNI and nothing sent but the handshake. Whether the certificate is valid for the name, who issued it, valid from and until with the days left (a warning under 30, a failure

tools.name: mttr_changes
tools.description: What the latest run of a site changed against the run before it: the score, rules now passing, rules newly failing, and pages added and removed. Call it after a rescan is done. For a site whose server sends its own counts, "visits" sets people, people an assistant sent and crawler fetches in the wee

tools.name: mttr_rescan
tools.description: Asks mttr to read a site again, after it has been changed. Returns a job to watch with mttr_job. A site is read at most once every ten minutes.

tools.name: mttr_citations
tools.description: What assistants were found to cite for a site, question by question, from lookups already made, and the credits left for more. Costs nothing.

tools.name: mttr_cite
tools.description: Asks ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity one question with web search on, and says whether each cites the site, where, whether it names it without citing it, and who it cites instead. Paid in mttr credits; mttr_citations shows the price and the balance first. Only the assistants mttr is connected to are

tools.name: mttr_signup
tools.description: Signs the person up with their email, the one call that works before mttr has a key for them. It answers their key, shown once, and the command that connects with it. Connect again with the key: it reads any public site’s report at once, and claiming their site with mttr_claim adds its private parts

tools.name: mttr_claim
tools.description: Starts claiming a site for the person: the TXT record or the file that proves they control it. Put either one up, then call mttr_claim_check. A claimed site joins their account: its Search Console figures, visits, citations and rivals, their work board and their progress page. Any key reads a site’s

tools.name: mttr_claim_check
tools.description: Checks the record or file from mttr_claim and, once it is found, adds the site to the person's account. A new DNS record can take a few minutes to be seen.

tools.name: mttr_list
tools.description: Names a site the person has claimed on the public leaderboard, with a link to its report, or with show false takes its name off again so it goes by an anonymous code. Only a claimed site can be named.

tools.name: mttr_log_work
tools.description: Tells mttr what you did on a site, after each step: what you planned, changed, checked, or where you got stuck, what you found along the way, the files you touched and the rules you worked on. It shows on your person’s progress page, and mttr reads these to get better. Never send secrets or a site’s

tools.name: mttr_approvals_set
tools.description: Sets how you work on one of the person's claimed sites: automatic, where you deploy each change as you go, or approve, where you propose each change with mttr_propose and deploy it only once the person approves. Turning approve off is emailed to the person. mttr_proposals({ site }) says which a site

tools.name: mttr_propose
tools.description: Before you deploy a change to a site set to approve, proposes it to the person: mttr keeps it and emails them what the change is, the rule and pages, your summary marked as your words, and an Approve and a Decline link, each working once and lapsing after 72 hours. Then wait: call mttr_proposal with

tools.name: mttr_proposal
tools.description: Where one proposal stands: pending, approved, declined or expired, with "deploy" true only once the person approved it, and their reason when they declined. Poll it every few minutes after mttr_propose; deploy only when it says approved.

tools.name: mttr_proposals
tools.description: The person's proposals, newest first, each with where it stands, for one site or all of them. With a site, it also says whether that site is set to approve or automatic: check it before you start work on a site.

tools.name: mttr_todo
tools.description: The person's work across their sites, as their progress page shows it: the next fix to make, with the words to work from, then every other fix by worth, what slipped back, what a read has checked fixed, and sites changed since their last read that need reading again. A fix counts as done only once a

tools.name: mttr_content_brain
tools.description: A claimed site's content brain as files to save under .mttr/brain/ in its repository: what the business does and where, how its pages read, the facts its structured data states, what is worth writing, and every brief so far. Read it before writing any page.

tools.name: mttr_content_next
tools.description: The brief for the page most worth writing next on a claimed site: the question, why, the kind of page and its path, the facts to use, the voice, and the rules it will be held to. mttr does not write the page; you or your person do. At most three briefs are open at once. When the page is live, call m

tools.name: mttr_content_done
tools.description: Says where a content brief's page went on the site, by the brief's id from mttr_content_next and the page's path. The brief goes live when a later read finds that page, and keeps where the site stood then. Ask for a read with mttr_rescan after.

tools.name: mttr_content_drop
tools.description: Drops one of your open content briefs for a site, by its id, freeing its place among the three open at once. A dropped brief is never handed out again.

tools.name: mttr_content_posts
tools.description: Briefs for posts about a page that went live from one of your content briefs: for X and for LinkedIn, the point of the page, one fact of the site's own that carries it, the link, the voice, and the characters left (X counts a link as 23). mttr writes no post and posts nothing; you or your person wri

tools.name: mttr_queue
tools.description: What the person queued for you from their mttr, oldest first: each task with its id, its site, and the words to work from. Check it when you start, and whenever an answer says tasks are waiting.

tools.name: mttr_queue_done
tools.description: Says a queued task is done, by its id from mttr_queue. The fix itself counts only once a later read finds it passing, so ask for a fresh read with mttr_rescan.

tools.name: mttr_progress_link
tools.description: A private link to the person's progress page: their sites, every read, what each changed, and what this agent has asked. Signed with this key; it lapses after the days asked (30 if none, 90 at most) or when the key is rotated. Hand it only to the person.

tools.name: mttr_portfolio
tools.description: The person's portfolio, private to them: one score across every site they have claimed, half for what was improved while they held each site, three tenths for where the sites stand now, and a fifth for search traffic, not counted yet. Every site by its real name with what it gives each part and why,

tools.name: mttr_portfolio_set
tools.description: Changes the person's portfolio: publish or hide it, a display name (shown as chosen by its holder, not checked; null clears it), a home site that says who is behind it (one of their sites proved by DNS or a file), or whether one site is named on it or goes by its code. A site is named only where its

tools.name: mttr_portfolio_veto
tools.description: For the owner of a site: takes it out of every portfolio but their own, at once, or with out false puts it back. Needs the site proved with this key by DNS or a file. To keep a site in portfolios but take its name off, call mttr_list with show false.

tools.name: mttr_job
tools.description: How a rescan stands: waiting, running, done or failed, and how many reads are ahead of it.

tools.name: mttr_events
tools.description: The newest things that happened: reads asked for, finished and failed, scores that moved, rules that were fixed.

tools.name: mttr_crawls
tools.description: The crawl as it stands: the sites being read now, the next in line, and how the reads that ended over the last 1, 7 or 30 days ended.

tools.name: mttr_links
tools.description: The links of a site from its latest run: broken ones by default, or all, those in page content, or the other sites linked to. Link text read from the site comes under "quoted".

tools.name: mttr_topics
tools.description: What a site covers: its subjects and the pages under each, pages competing for the same search, and places a subject is missing from. A model named the subjects, so names come under "quoted".

tools.name: mttr_structure
tools.description: How a site is put together: its sections, how many clicks each sits from the home page, how much of each is linked from page content, and the links between sections.

tools.name: mttr_map
tools.description: Every page of a site's latest read, one of three ways. tree: by address, folders as branches, each page with its state, failing rules, clicks from home and words. links: each page reached from home with its clicks and its first way in, the hubs, and the pages no link leads to (none named when the re

tools.name: mttr_compare
tools.description: Two sites already read, rule by rule: the scores and stages side by side, and the rules each is ahead or behind on by the share of its pages passing. With view "content", their content by meaning instead: their pages measured, page pairs both write about with words on each, and what only one of them

tools.name: mttr_reviews
tools.description: Verdicts a model could not be relied on for, which wait for a person and count neither for nor against a score. Only sites with something waiting, a screen at a time, newest read first, with the total across every site. What the model recorded comes under "quotedDetail".

tools.name: mttr_rules
tools.description: The rulebook: every rule mttr checks, with its stage, its weight and how to fix a failure.

tools.name: mttr_similar
tools.description: Pages of a site that mean nearly the same thing, grouped, which may compete for one search. With a path, the pages nearest that page, each with the two passages that come closest. Read from vectors of the page text, so the site must have been embedded. Passages come under "quoted".

tools.name: mttr_near
tools.description: The sites closest in meaning to one site, closest first: the ones writing about the same work, which are its likeliest rivals. Read from one vector a site kept in the catalog, so both sites must have been embedded.

tools.name: mttr_leaderboard
tools.description: The public leaderboard: every ranked site by the score of its latest read, places shared on a tie, or the board of one crowd: a line of work with "in", a state, a city in that state, a size, or any of them together, each place counted as a site's report counts it. Each with its stages, pages read an

tools.name: mttr_explore
tools.description: One thing mttr knows and every way on from it, each edge marked by what made it: meaning (close in meaning, never better or cited), links (pages linking between sites, or between pages of one site, with their anchor text) or rules (code checking pages against the rulebook). Across sites: a site, a m

tools.name: mttr_markets
tools.description: The markets last found: groups of sites close in meaning, each named by the site at its centre, largest first. A site in a market is writing about the same work as the others in it.

tools.name: mttr_search
tools.description: Ask a question, such as a buyer would, and get the passages that answer it best, and each site once by its best passage under "bySite", from the sites closest to the question, one market, or named sites. At most 12 sites are read. Passages come under "quoted". Close means similar in meaning, not rig

tools.name: mttr_examples
tools.description: How other sites pass a page rule a page fails: pages on sites in the same market, or the nearest sites, that pass the rule and are closest to the page in meaning, each with the passage that comes closest. Worked examples for writing the fix. Passages come under "quoted".

tools.name: mttr_market
tools.description: A site set against its market, or its nearest sites when it has none: its place by score, the median score, and for every rule the share of pages passing here against the market median and the best site, with the rules furthest behind first.

tools.name: mttr_gaps
tools.description: Content gaps: subjects a site’s rivals write about that nothing on the site comes close to in meaning, the one most rivals cover first, each with the rival pages and the nearest page here. Page titles come under "quoted".

tools.name: mttr_tells
tools.description: The signs of generated text on a site's pages: hidden characters that can carry a watermark or hidden instructions (with any message spelled out in tag characters), chat and markdown left in, placeholders never filled in, stock phrasing, and heavy use of dashes. Strong signs first. A sign is not pro

tools.name: mttr_competitors
tools.description: A site's competitors: where it is (from the address or phone numbers on its own pages), the sites near it that do similar work by meaning, everyone near it, and sites doing similar work elsewhere, each with score, pages, and how many sites read link to it, against the site's own.

tools.name: mttr_backlinks
tools.description: The sites mttr has read that link to a site, the most pages first, with how many sites were counted. Links from sites mttr has not read are not known.

tools.name: mttr_traffic
tools.description: Clicks from Google search, from Search Console. With no site, every site read from Search Console with its clicks and impressions against as many days before, and the searches nothing on two or more of the sites answers, grouped by subject. With a site: clicks by day, the totals against as many days

tools.name: mttr_visits
tools.description: Who fetched a site's pages in the last 28 days against the 28 before, counted by the site's own server: people, people an assistant such as ChatGPT or Perplexity sent, and crawlers by name, AI crawlers marked. By day, by crawler, by assistant and by page, with the last day an AI crawler fetched each

tools.name: mttr_queries
tools.description: The searches Google showed a site's pages for, from Search Console, with clicks, impressions and average place: by query, by page, or only those close to the top (places 4 to 20). Only sites whose owner added mttr in Search Console have any. Queries come under "quoted".

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "mttr_log_work" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: mttr_product_check, mttr_reviews · Private data: mttr_agent_view, mttr_signup, mttr_claim, mttr_claim_check, mttr_log_work, mttr_content_brain, mttr_progress_link, mttr_portfolio, mttr_portfolio_set, mttr_portfolio_veto, mttr_leaderboard · Public sink: mttr_site, mttr_locations, mttr_signup, mttr_log_work, mttr_content_posts, mttr_portfolio_set, mttr_compare, mttr_market · Destructive: mttr_site, mttr_pages, mttr_changes, mttr_content_drop, mttr_links.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: mttr_product_check, mttr_reviews · Private data: mttr_agent_view, mttr_signup, mttr_claim, mttr_claim_check, mttr_log_work, mttr_content_brain, mttr_progress_link, mttr_portfolio, mttr_portfolio_set, mttr_portfolio_veto, mttr_leaderboard · Public sink: mttr_site, mttr_locations, mttr_signup, mttr_log_work, mttr_content_posts, mttr_portfolio_set, mttr_compare, mttr_market · Destructive: mttr_site, mttr_pages, mttr_changes, mttr_content_drop, mttr_links

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
